articles.title: SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
articles.snippet:
SolaREIT has surpassed $8.5 billion in project value supported through its real estate financing, covering approximately 4.6 gigawatts of solar and battery storage capacity.
The post SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:56 PM
SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
SolaREIT has surpassed $8.5 billion in project value supported through its real estate financing, covering approximately 4.6 gigawatts of solar and battery storage capacity.
The milestone represents more than $3.5 billion in additional project value since November 2025. It measures the value of associated energy projects rather than the amount of financing directly provided by SolaREIT.
The Virginia-based company offers land purchases, lease purchases and land loans across all 50 states.
Its services cover utility-scale and distributed solar, battery energy storage and related infrastructure, including substation and transmission land.
The model allows developers and project owners to access capital tied to project real estate. Management said that flexibility is important when financing conditions, procurement plans and interconnection schedules change.
Co-Founder and CEO Laura Pagliarulo described land as an asset developers can use to raise capital in a constrained funding environment.
Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer Laura Klein said transactions can close within 30 to 45 days of signing, using diligence built around information developers already hold about their projects.
Founded in 2020 as a real estate investment trust, SolaREIT is a woman-owned and led business established by clean energy industry executives.
Its team brings experience across project development, finance, real estate and community solar. The company works with both developers and landowners.
The milestone reflects growth in real estate financing as one component of renewable energy project funding.
SolaREIT’s offering focuses specifically on land, providing developers with an additional source of capital alongside the other financing needed to build and operate solar, storage and associated infrastructure.
The company said its team’s industry experience helps it evaluate complex transactions and structure financing around project timelines.
KEY QUOTES:
“We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to developers and project owners, helping them create additional value in a capital-constrained environment. It’s been another turbulent year, with higher interest rates and shifting policy, and the land under their projects is one of the few assets developers can turn into capital quickly. Surpassing $8.5 billion in project value financed reflects the trust our partners place in us. Our team has over 300 years of collective experience in the clean energy space, which allows us to help developers finance even their most complex deals.”
Laura Pagliarulo, Co-Founder And CEO Of SolaREIT
“In this market, speed and flexibility matter. With interconnection deadlines and procurement plans constantly shifting, developers need capital solutions that work on their timeline. We build our diligence on what developers already know about their projects, so we can close in 30 to 45 days from signing, providing developers with capital on a schedule they can plan around.”
Laura Klein, Chief Financial Officer And Chief Operating Officer Of SolaREIT

articles.title: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
articles.snippet:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.
The post Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:04 PM
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.
The acquisition represents the recently listed company’s first investment and carries an initial capitalization rate of 7%. The joint ventures will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses.
AWS will retain a 25% interest in the ventures and lease the entire portfolio on a triple-net basis. The initial lease term is 12 years, with extensions potentially taking the total term to 32 years.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions.
The investment establishes a starting portfolio aligned with the trust’s strategy of acquiring stabilized data centers leased to major cloud providers under long-term contracts.
CEO and President Nick Pell identified asset quality, pricing and the tenant relationship as reasons for deploying proceeds from the company’s initial public offering into the portfolio.
For AWS, the arrangement combines continued occupancy with minority ownership. The company said the partnership supports its expansion while maintaining its focus on local employment, workforce training and community priorities.
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust targets newly constructed, income-generating facilities leased to investment-grade hyperscale tenants. Its strategy emphasizes contractual cash flows, rent increases and further acquisitions.
The company is externally managed by a Blackstone affiliate. Blackstone manages nearly $1.4 trillion across real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure and other strategies.
Morgan Stanley, CBRE Capital Markets, Citi, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Wells Fargo are serving as financial advisors on the transaction. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett is advising Blackstone legally.
KEY QUOTES
“We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation. The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.”
Nick Pell, CEO And President Of Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust
“As we scale to meet growing demand for our customers, we’re committed to building in a way that strengthens the communities where we operate. We’re focused on delivering long-term local benefits, from creating good jobs and free workforce training programs to supporting local priorities. Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build.”
Prasad Kalyanaraman, Vice President Of AWS Infrastructure

India's artificial intelligence (AI) startup ecosystem has attracted approximately $1.91 billion across 102 funding rounds between January 1 and November 5, 2026, with a handful of large-ticket transactions accounting for a significant portion of the capital raised, according to data compiled by Tracxn .
The funding activity includes investments across companies developing AI infrastructure, generative AI platforms and enterprise applications, with some of the largest transactions involving businesses operating in the infrastructure and computing ecosystem.
Advt
Neysa's $600 million Series B round in February was the largest funding transaction recorded during the period. Sarvam followed with a $255.1 million Series B round in June, while semiconductor technology company Kandou raised $225 million through a Series E round in March.
Other significant transactions included Yotta's $150 million Series D round in July and Emergent's $130 million Series C round in the same month. Emergent had also raised $70 million through a Series B round in January.
Sarvam subsequently raised another $90.4 million in August, while Freehand secured $75 million through a Series B round in July.
The four largest funding transactions — involving Neysa, Sarvam, Kandou and Yotta — together accounted for approximately $1.23 billion, or nearly 64 per cent of the total funding recorded during the period.
Peak XV Partners leads investor participation
Sarvam subsequently raised another $90.4 million in August, while Freehand secured $75 million through a Series B round in July. On the investor side, Peak XV Partners emerged as the most active investor in India's AI startup funding landscape, participating in six funding rounds during the period.
Khosla Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Together, Info Edge Ventures, Capital 2B, IvyCap Ventures, Antler, Venture Catalysts and Wyser followed, with participation in three rounds each.
Advt
In terms of lead-investor participation, Peak XV Partners led three funding rounds, while IvyCap Ventures and Info Edge Ventures led two rounds each.
The investor activity reflects participation by established venture capital firms, as well as funds backing emerging AI companies at different stages of development.
The funding rounds recorded during the period included seed, Series A, Series B, and later-stage investments, as well as venture debt, conventional debt, and grant-related entries.

Plural Raises USD 1.1 Billion to Invest in Europe's AI, Robotics and Defense Startups
Plural, a UK venture firm, raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. Two-thirds goes to early-stage startups, and the rest backs current portfolio companies. It targets energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare. Six tech founders and executives lead the firm.
Written By:
Murali Teja
Reviewed By:
Manisha Sharma
Published on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Updated on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Copied
UK-based venture capital firm Plural has raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. The money will back technology startups across Europe. The firm plans to focus on energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare.
The new fund shows that investors are paying more attention to European tech. Many of them want companies that build tools for key industries.
Pural Sets its Investment Priorities
Plural will put two-thirds of the fund into early-stage startups. The rest will go to companies it already backs. This extra money will help them grow.
The firm wants to find startups that can become large businesses. Its list of interests is wide. It includes AI infrastructure, chip making, the factories that produce chips, robotics and defense technology.
The firm does not plan to bet on just one area. It wants to back founders who know their field well and who want to build companies that compete around the world.
Six Partners Lead Plural's Investment Strategy
A group of tech founders and business leaders started Plural in 2022. Since then, it has invested in several European companies . These include Helsing, Proxima Fusion, OLIX and The Exploration Company.
Six partners lead the firm. They are Taavet Hinrikus, who co-founded Wise, and Sten Tamkivi, who co-founded Teleport. Ian Hogarth, who co-founded Songkick, is also a partner. So is Khaled Helioui, a former chief executive of Bigpoint. Carina Namih, who co-founded HelixNano, and Pierre-Dimitri Gore-Coty, a former Uber executive, complete the team.
Hinrikus said the firm has no fixed view on which sector will produce the next big company. Instead, the partners want to work with founders who have deep knowledge of their own industries.

A Boost for Europe's Strategic Technology Ambitions
The new fund adds fresh money to Europe's startup scene. Its focus on energy, chips, robotics and defense also fits a wider need. Europe wants stronger industry and more control over key technology.
For founders, the news means more support is available as they try to grow. For Plural, it means more room to back new ideas and to stand by the companies already in its portfolio.

The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The post Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:29 AM
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
Sofinnova Partners, a European life sciences venture capital firm, has completed the final close of Sofinnova Crossover II at €725 million, equivalent to approximately $815 million. The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The new vehicle is expected to support approximately 15 companies over its investment period.
While its primary focus will be Europe, the fund will also pursue selected opportunities in the United States and other international markets.
Sofinnova believes the successful fundraising reflects increasing investor confidence in European life sciences businesses developing technologies with global commercial potential.
The fund will provide capital to companies approaching important stages of clinical development and business growth.
Supporting Clinical Development And Commercialization
Life sciences companies frequently require substantial financing to advance experimental therapies and medical technologies through clinical testing, regulatory approval, and commercialization.
Sofinnova Crossover II is designed to support businesses during these later stages of development.
Its investment strategy focuses on companies with promising scientific foundations, clinical validation, and leadership teams capable of expanding internationally.
Sofinnova believes the European market is producing an increasing number of competitive healthcare companies that need access to substantial growth capital.
The firm’s investment approach combines financial backing with industry expertise and strategic support.
Building On Crossover I
Sofinnova’s first crossover fund invested in several companies that subsequently completed significant corporate transactions or public market milestones.
These include LimFlow, acquired by Inari Medical; Calliditas Therapeutics, acquired by Asahi Kasei; and Amolyt Pharma, acquired by AstraZeneca.
The portfolio also included Abivax, which achieved a Nasdaq listing.
These investments demonstrate the firm’s strategy of backing life sciences companies as they advance toward larger commercial markets.
Crossover II has already invested in Hemab Therapeutics, CellCentric, and Neurent Medical.
The fund will continue seeking opportunities among biotechnology and medical technology companies with differentiated products and clinical development programs.
Investment Leadership And Institutional Support
The Crossover II strategy is led by Sofinnova partners Joe Anderson, Kinam Hong, Cedric Moreau, Jacques Theurillat, and David Evans.
The fund is supported by the European Tech Champions Initiative, a fund-of-funds managed by the European Investment Fund.
Sofinnova Partners was founded in 1972 and operates from Paris, London, and Milan.
The firm has invested in more than 500 companies across its history and currently manages more than €4 billion in assets.
Its investment activities span life sciences and sustainability, from early-stage company formation through later-stage development.

articles.title: JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
articles.snippet:
JBS has agreed to acquire Brazilian consumer products company Flora for $542 million, expanding into beauty and personal care while adding to its household cleaning business.
The post JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:20 PM
JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
JBS has agreed to acquire Brazilian consumer products company Flora for $542 million, expanding into beauty and personal care while adding to its household cleaning business.
Flora is owned by J&F Group, JBS’s controlling shareholder. The transaction therefore brings a business from its controlling shareholder into the company.
The purchase includes assumed debt, with $367 million in equity consideration payable entirely through JBS treasury Class A shares, Brazilian depositary receipts or a combination of both.
JBS expects no change to its net leverage ratio based on Flora’s earnings contribution and the transaction structure.
Flora generated R$2.9 billion, approximately $531 million, in annual net revenue for the 12 months ended September 2026. Its brands include Minuano, Francis, Neutrox and OX.
The company operates five factories, seven distribution centers and a research and development center, employing more than 4,200 people.
Flora originated as JBS’s hygiene and cleaning division before separating in 2007. The businesses have maintained commercial ties, including JBS’s supply of beef tallow for cleaning and hygiene products.
JBS intends to connect its ingredients and collagen capabilities with Flora’s brands, distribution and consumer products expertise.
The acquisition complements Genu-in, established in 2022 to develop collagen applications, and research activities at JBS Biotech and BioTech Foods.
JBS also announced an $11 million acquisition of Canal Rural, an agribusiness-focused Brazilian media company, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The final price will be adjusted for closing net debt.
Both acquisitions are expected to close in December 2026, subject to customary conditions.
The transactions broaden JBS’s activities beyond its global food portfolio, with Flora providing an established platform for expansion into adjacent consumer categories.
